title: Yash's 'Toxic' Closes Week One at Rs 314 Crore Worldwide Amid Profitability Concerns
excerpt: Despite crossing Rs 300 crore worldwide in seven days, steep daily drops and an estimated Rs 300-400 crore budget have trade analysts questioning whether the Kannada blockbuster can turn profitable.
body:
• Yash's "Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown Ups" closed its first week with Rs 229.95 crore net in India and Rs 313.55 crore worldwide, powered by a massive Rs 101.10 crore opening day.
  • Hindi collections account for roughly Rs 123-125 crore of the domestic total, but daily drops have been steep — from Rs 50 crore on Day 1 to Rs 4 crore by the first Monday.
  • With an estimated production budget of Rs 300-400 crore, the film needs to cross Rs 500 crore worldwide to be profitable, according to trade analysts.
  • Week two faces additional pressure from the September 4 theatrical release of "Mirzapur: The Movie," which targets the same Hindi-belt audience.

Yash's Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown Ups wrapped its first week of release with a worldwide gross of Rs 313.55 crore, according to Sacnilk data. The Kannada-language film, directed by Geetu Mohandas, collected Rs 229.95 crore net domestically across all languages, with an additional Rs 40.75 crore from overseas markets.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=f5M1d7r2UNQ

The numbers tell two stories at once. In absolute terms, a Rs 300 crore-plus first week is a significant commercial performance by Indian cinema standards. But against the film's estimated production budget of Rs 300-400 crore — a figure cited by trade analyst Rohit Jaiswal — the trajectory raises serious questions about profitability.

A Record Opening, Then a Steep Slide

Toxic opened on August 26 to Rs 101.10 crore net in India across 24,579 shows, benefiting from a mid-week holiday. The number was among the biggest non-holiday openings in Indian cinema history. But the decline was immediate and relentless: Rs 37.65 crore on Day 2, Rs 27.20 crore on Day 3, Rs 25.15 crore on Day 4, and Rs 23 crore on Day 5.

The post-weekend correction hit hard. Day 6 (Monday) dropped 66.7% from Sunday to Rs 7.65 crore. Day 7 showed a minor 7.2% uptick to Rs 8.20 crore across 12,894 shows, but by then the daily run rate had fallen to less than a tenth of opening day.

Hindi Belt Drives the Numbers — and the Worry

The Hindi-language version has been Toxic's strongest market, contributing roughly Rs 123-125 crore of the domestic total through seven days, per trade estimates. Bollywood Hungama's day-wise tracking shows Hindi collections fell from Rs 50.31 crore on Day 1 to Rs 4.09 crore by Day 6 and Rs 4.05 crore on Day 7, an occupancy-led "discounted Tuesday" that failed to generate a meaningful bounce.

"Toxic is turning out to be one of the worst trending films of all time, on the lines of the Aamir Khan-led Thugs of Hindostan."

— Bollywood Hungama

Industry projections suggest the Hindi run may end around Rs 150 crore lifetime — a figure that would be respectable for most dubbed releases but falls short given the scale of investment. Kannada and other South Indian language versions have contributed smaller shares, with Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam collectively adding single-digit daily figures during the weekdays.

Can It Reach the Rs 500 Crore Mark?

Trade analysts have pegged Rs 500 crore worldwide as the threshold Toxic needs to cross for profitability. With Rs 313.55 crore in the bank after seven days, the film would need its second and third weeks to collectively add nearly Rs 190 crore — a tall order given the current trajectory.

The challenge intensifies on September 4 with the theatrical release of Mirzapur: The Movie, which directly targets the Hindi-belt audience that has been Toxic's primary market. Screen allocation is expected to shift, further compressing Toxic's remaining run.

Directed by Geetu Mohandas, Toxic features Yash in a dual role alongside an ensemble cast including Nayanthara, Kiara Advani, Huma Qureshi, Tara Sutaria and Rukmini Vasanth. The film was produced jointly by KVN Productions and Monster Mind Creations, with production handled by Venkat K. Narayana and Yash.

What the Numbers Mean

The debate around Toxic's commercial fate underscores a wider tension in Indian cinema: massive opening-day numbers driven by star power and advance booking hype do not guarantee sustained theatrical runs. Word of mouth, which has been mixed to negative for Toxic, remains the decisive factor beyond the first weekend.

Kantara composer Ajaneesh Loknath pushed back on the narrative, urging fans to watch the film in theatres before forming an opinion and comparing the reception debate to that around Aamir Khan's Lagaan. "Don't just read reviews, experience cinema," he said. Whether the second weekend brings a recovery or confirms the downward trend will determine where Toxic ultimately lands in the hit-or-flop ledger.
